about: Curated evidence for cells where the materialised noun oracle disagrees with the engine and an external authority settles it. This is not dictionary data: each rule names the source. Loaded by tools/illegal_evidence.py and gated by tools/test_illegal_evidence.py.

rules.note: simmarit has the short plural simmareitta, not the oracle's simmariteitta
rääppeet has the short plural rääppeittä, not the oracle's rääppeeeittä
class-7 plural-only -t words use the stem without the nominative -t (suitsitta, happiviiksittä, päitsittä, saksitta); the oracle concatenates the nominative
kiittimet has the short plural kiittimittä, not the oracle's kiittimmemittä

class-51 compounds keep the modifier in the nominative (kuiva + kakku, oma + kuva); the oracle inflects the modifier into the middle of the word (kuiviinkakkuihinsa, omittakuvitta), which is not the only paradigm
a case-less possessive reading is checked against the nominative cell; the engine also emits the correct nominative possessive (omakuvani, mustamakkarani)
raskas/vieras have the genitive-plural variants raskasten/raskaiden/raskaitten and vierasten/vieraiden/vieraiten; raskastensarjojen and vierastenmiehien are valid rare forms the oracle's set omits
a case-less possessive reading is checked against the nominative cell; mustaherukkaani is the partitive possessive and mustaherukkani the nominative, and both are emitted
class-50 compounds keep the modifier fixed or use its genitive-plural variant (raskas/raskaiden, pitkä/pitkättä, raitis/raittiiden); the engine's form is the compound reading
koi has the illative koihin; the oracle's koihan/koihen are the class-18 alternatives, not the only reading

these classes carry pluralia tantum whose citation form is the nominative plural (aktiivat, rintsikat, menkat, perskat, markkinat); the engine declines the dropped-`t` base and strong-grades it back where the class gradates (aktiivoiden, rintsikoiden, menkkojen), while the oracle builds every plural cell from the nominative plural (aktiivatiden, rintsikatiden, menkatiden)

a comparative's -mpi takes the weak -mm- grade in the open-syllable cases (alamaisemman, alamaisemmalta, alamaisemmatta; kuurommalta; krouvimmalta), and the strong -mpa- belongs only to the nominative, partitive, illative and essive; the oracle sometimes keeps the strong grade in the weak cells (alamaisempalta, kuurompalta, krouvimpalta), which is not a word

a class-38 -iset noun (avajaiset, läksiäiset, kuukautiset) is the nominative plural of an -inen singular and Wiktionary marks it plural-only ({{monikollinen}}, yks=-); the engine declines the singular and keeps only the plural cells, while the oracle still claims the singular

the -i loanwords take the maa-type singular obliques (piitä, piissä, piiltä, piiksi; koita, koissa; täitä, täissä) and Wiktionary lists them; Omorfi generates only the plural, so the engine's correct singular forms have neither oracle and are reported unsupported
laki accepts both lakini and lakeni as the nominative possessive; the oracle lists only the strong-stem spelling
the 48-E noun is the dialectal lipeä with genitive lipeen; the oracle's livenne belongs to the separate class-8 loanword homonym
live Voikko reads the engine's säkene- forms as this lemma; a Wiktionary citation is still to be added
taival's plural illative is the taipale- family; the oracle's taipali- spelling is not the word
havas is a dual-class word; the engine's hapaa- possessive forms are one valid paradigm
class-41 plural-only and comparative forms keep the short stem (valjaitta, rynttyittä, lunnaitta); the oracle inserts extra material (valjaaitta, rynttyyittä) or the comparative stem (valmiimpattaan)
fudut/chinot are plural-only class-1 words; fuduitta/chinoitta are the short abessive plurals, not fudutitta/chinotitta
tikkaat has the short abessive plural tikkaitta, not tikkaaitta
aterimet has the short abessive plural aterimitta, not aterimemitta
hohtimet has the short abessive plural hohtimitta, not hohtimemitta
class-39 plural-only -t words use the stem without the nominative -t (kiduksitta, toveruksitta); the oracle concatenates the nominative
class-18 -i loanwords take the illative -hin (pak-choihin, bihin); the oracle offers -han/-hen alternatives
pak-choin is the genitive singular; the case-less reading is checked against the nominative cell, whose correct form pak-choi is also emitted
hyphenated/compound class-51 words keep the established modifier spelling (nuoritta-isännittä, mustainraamattujen); the oracle's inserted material is not a word

mustaviinimarja is musta + viini + marja; the engine now splits the compound-like middle tail and inflects the first part and the head (mustanviinimarjan, mustiinviinimarjoihin), while the oracle's expected set for the multi-part compound is a combinatorial split of its own (mudtaviinienkuiden, mustaviinimarjiinkuihin)
kipsaasi is the partitive possessive; the case-less reading is checked against the nominative cell, whose correct form kipsasi is also emitted
the engine's instructive plural or partitive possessive of a plural-only -t lemma is checked against the nominative cell; the correct nominative form is also emitted
suorakulmio/suoraommel have head variants (kulmio/kulmi-, ommel/ompel-) that the oracle's set omits

these are plural-only compounds whose tail is the nominative plural of a lemma (vanhemmat/vanhempi, olot/olo, kustannukset/kustannus, sisarukset/sisarus); the engine inflects that plural paradigm (isovanhemmitta, omakustannuksitta), while the oracle either concatenates the nominative (isovanhemmatitta) or uses the singular genitive stem (omakustannukseitta)
the engine's partitive plural possessive (pässinpökkimiänsä) is the real form; the oracle's pässinpökkimätään concatenates the nominative
silkkivuori/tikkivuori/villiviini NOM possessive readings are case-less; the correct nominative possessive is also emitted
mustatorvisieni/vapaataival have head variants (torvisieni, taipale-), and pitkäperjantai accepts both pitkä- and pitkään-; the oracle's set omits the engine's forms
kiiru has the kiiruun and kiireen possessive stems; the oracle lists only the kiiruun spelling

a class-51 compound whose first part is the nominative plural of its head (isot + aivot, pitkät + housut) is plural-only, and the engine now inflects both parts in the plural (isojenaivojen, isojaaivoja, pitkienhousujen). The oracle's expected set for these long compounds is a split of unrelated parts (isotoittamerittä, pitkäthouenkuiden), which is not a word

the head is the participle särkynyt (broken), which is not a sanalista lemma; the class-47 engine inflects it, so the paradigm is särkyneensydämen, särkyneetsydämet, särkyneittäsydämittä. The oracle's expected set is a split of unrelated parts (särkynytöillämerillä, särkynyillesärjöille)

a consonant-final loan builds the plural instructive as i-stem + -n (gourmetin, nougatin), which is the same word as the genitive singular. Merging the two readings leaves the form with neither case tag, and the report's least-assuming candidate is the nominative cell. Both readings are correct, so the case-less form is not an invented nominative.
Wiktionary gives the plural elative as aavoistameristä; the oracle expects the inessive aavoissamerissä for the same cell. The engine form is the recorded elative.
Wiktionary lists hienojensokerien, hienojensokereiden and hienojensokereitten; the oracle keeps only the first two, so hienojensokereiden is an oracle omission.
kuusi has both kuusien and kuusten in the genitive plural; hopeakuusi inherits both, so hopeakuusten is not an engine defect.
kuve gradates v -> p and its plural ablative is kupeilta; live Voikko analyses kupeilta as a form of kuve. The oracle's kuveilta is a different word/entry.
mies has both miesten and miehien genitive plurals, so mustienmiehien and mustienmiesten are both valid compound forms.

isosisar is iso + sisar; the modifier-inflected genitive plural isojensisarien uses the head isojen with the tail's isosisarien, and live Voikko accepts it. The oracle records only isojensisarten; the other two spellings in this cell are covered by compound-51-fixed-prefix.
livenne is a form of the verb livetä, not the noun live; the noun's gradating stem gives lipeenne. The oracle is mixing the verb into the noun's cell.

Wiktionary's omena declension gives the i-stem plural beside the o-stem: algebrien, algebria, algebriin, algebrissa, algebrista, algebrilla, algebrilta, algebrille, algebrina, algebriksi, algebritta, algebroin. The oracle records those rows as Omorfi-only because Voikko's dictionary has only the o-stem, so the engine's i-stem column is real but not ok='both'.

Wiktionary gives vyyhti both the 7*F ovi and the 5*F risti declension. The oracle generated only the 7*F column and wrote the 5*F plural (vyyhdit, vyyhteinä, vyyhteihin, vyyhdeittä, ...) as engine rows, so the engine's risti plural is real but not ok='both'.

Wiktionary's pahahenki entry is the closed alt form of paha henki, and its fi-decl-kala-ovi|space= table gives the weak nominative singular possessives pahahenkeni, pahahenkesi, pahahenkemme, pahahenkenne and pahahenkensä (the henki table agrees). The oracle's strong pahahenkini/pahahenkisi/pahahenkimme/pahahenkinne are Voikko-accepted alternates, not the standard forms, so they are oracle-only.

Wiktionary gives laki two declensions: the law noun as 5*D risti (lain, lakia, laissa, laitta, lait, lakien, lakeja, lakeihin, laeissa, ...) and the summit/ceiling noun as 7*D ovi (laen, lakea, laessa, laetta, laet, lakien, lakia, lakiin, laissa, ...). The materialised oracle wrote the 5*D paradigm as ok='both' on both homonym rows and the 7*D forms as engine-only, so the 7*D bucket expects the 5*D forms. Both paradigms are real; the engine emits the 7*D one in this bucket.

Wiktionary gives kuusi two paradigms: the numeral six as 27 käsi (kuuden, kuutta, kuudetta, ...) and the spruce noun as 24 uni (kuusen, kuusta, kuusetta, ...). The materialised oracle wrote the numeral forms as ok='both' on both homonym rows, so the class-24 bucket expects them. They belong to the class-27 numeral, which is reported separately.

The engine's kuusen/kuusta/kuusetta column is the class-24 spruce paradigm (Wiktionary's fi-decl-uni|kuus|a). The oracle's expected kuuden/kuutta/kuudetta in the same cells are the class-27 numeral forms, which the same page gives as fi-decl-käsi. Both are real; this rule explains the cross-homonym spelling.

Wiktionary's katiska declension gives porina both plural families: genitive plural porinoiden/porinoitten/porinojen and partitive plural porinoita/porinoja. The oracle lists only the i-plural, so the vowel-plural porinojen/porinoja is real but not ok='both'.

Wiktionary's askel table gives the plural illative as autereisiin/autereihin/auteriin, and mantereisiin/mantereihin/manteriin. The oracle lists only the -isiin spelling, so the -ihin alternates are real but not ok='both'.
Wiktionary's rosé table gives both singular illatives cowboyhin and cowboyhyn, and both third-person possessives cowboyhinsa and cowboyhynsa. The oracle lists only the -hin spelling.
Wiktionary's nainen-koira template gives the genitive plural as kultaistennoutajien/kultaisiennoutajien; the oracle lists only the first.

Wiktionary lists both the lämminruo- and lämminru- (ruu-) koira paradigms, and the materialised oracle confirms one variant per cell. Both the ruo- and ruu- forms are real, so the other variant is not an engine error.

Wiktionary gives HIV two pronunciations and paradigms: /hiʋ/ as 5 risti (HIVin, HIVittä) and /hoːiːʋeː/ as the filee-dot abbreviation (HIV:n, HIV:ttä). The sanalista row is 18,5, so the class-5 spellings are real forms of the same word, not class-18 errors.

Wiktionary gives two appi etymologies: the father-in-law as 7*B ovi (apen, appea) and the informal app as 5*B risti (apin, appia). The oracle's homonym rows share one form set, so the 5*B bucket sees the 7*B spellings as expected and the 5*B spellings as extra. Both paradigms are real.

Wiktionary gives two lahti etymologies: the bay as 7*F ovi (lahden, lahtea) and the second noun as 5*F risti (lahdin, lahtia). The oracle's homonym rows share one form set, so the 5*F bucket sees the 7*F spellings as expected and the 5*F spellings as extra. Both paradigms are real.
Wiktionary's katiska declension gives suurimoiden/suurimoitten/suurimojen, so the i-plural spellings are real even though the oracle lists only suurimojen.

Wiktionary's katiska declension gives both families for these -hina words: kohinoiden/kohinoitten/kohinojen, marinoiden/marinoitten/marinojen, kahinoiden/kahinoitten/kahinojen, kuhinoiden/kuhinoitten/kuhinojen and rahinoiden/rahinoitten/rahinojen. The oracle lists only the i-plural, so the vowel-plural spellings are real but not ok='both'.

Wiktionary's laatikko table gives both the strong poliitikkojen/poliitikkoja/poliitikkoihin and the weak poliitikoiden/poliitikoitten/poliitikoita/poliitikoihin. The oracle lists only the strong, so the weak i-plural and illative are real but not ok='both'; the weak essive poliitikoina is not in the table and is repaired.
Wiktionary's palvelu declension gives huitaisujen/huitaisuiden/huitaisuitten and huitaisuja/huitaisuita; the oracle lists only the vowel-plural, so the i-plural spellings are real but not ok='both'.

Wiktionary gives kylmäkalle as the nalle type: kylmäkallen, kylmäkallea, kylmäkalleja. The oracle's kylmäkalleen/kylmäkalletta cells are the hame type, not this word; the engine's nalle forms are the real ones.

Wiktionary's laatikko table gives both the strong eksentrikkojen/eksentrikkoja/eksentrikkoihin and the weak eksentrikoiden/eksentrikoitten/eksentrikoita/eksentrikoihin. The oracle lists only the strong, so the weak i-plural and illative are real but not ok='both'; the weak essive eksentrikoina is not in the table and is repaired.

Wiktionary's askel table gives the plural illative as penkereisiin/penkereihin/penkereisiin and kyyneleisiin/kyyneleihin; the oracle lists only the -isiin spelling, so the -ihin alternates are real but not ok='both'.
Wiktionary's rosé declension gives both singular illatives playboyhin and playboyhyn, and both third-person possessives playboyhinsa and playboyhynsa. The oracle lists only the -hin spelling.

Wiktionary gives handsfree only the front declension (fi-decl-rosé|handsfree|ä): handsfreeiltä, handsfreetä, handsfreehen. The materialised oracle wrote the back-harmony column (handsfreeilta, handsfreeansä), so the engine's front forms are the real ones and the oracle's back cells are oracle-only.
Wiktionary's solakka declension gives mustaherukoiden/mustaherukoitten/mustaherukkojen. The engine's weak i-plural forms are real; the oracle lists only the strong -kko- spelling.

Wiktionary's pieni-mies declension gives nuortenmiesten/nuortenmiehien/nuorienmiesten/nuorienmiehien. The oracle lists only nuorienmiehien, so the other genitive-plural combinations are real but not ok='both'.
The modifier kevyt has both kevyiden and kevyitten genitive-plural stems; the compound page's tail is kevytsarjojen, and the engine's kevyittensarjojen is the other standard head spelling.
Wiktionary's hame declension gives the plural illative as kyseisiin/kyseihin; the oracle lists only kyseisiin.

Wiktionary gives täysihoito as the valo type with t:d: täysihoidon, täysihoitoa, täysihoidoissa, täysihoidoilta. The oracle's strong tail cells (täysihoitoilta) are wrong; the engine's valo-f forms are the real ones.

Wiktionary gives two declensions: maa (pitkäperjantain) and koira-maa with both parts inflecting (pitkänperjantain). The engine's class-50 form is the maa one; the oracle's pitkänperjantain is the alternative, not a recall gap.

Wiktionary's laatikko table gives both the strong loogikkojen/loogikkoja/loogikkoihin and the weak loogikoiden/loogikoitten/loogikoita/loogikoihin (and likewise koirakko, suolakko). The oracle lists only the strong, so the weak i-plural and illative are real; the weak essive is repaired by the class engine.
